content.thinking:
The recent series of actions have successfully reconfigured all agents to use the Groq local adapter with the compound model and proper environment variables. I also patched the Groq adapter's timeout handling to treat a timeoutSec of 0 as “no timeout” rather than aborting immediately, and reinstalled the patched adapter (now version 0.7.0 under the new path groq-paperclip-adapter-r3). The installation response indicated that a restart is required for the changes to take effect.

The user’s last message shows that a task (GLI-19) is blocked and the UI reported a timeout after 0 seconds. This is exactly the symptom the zero‑timeout bug caused. Since I have already applied the fix and installed the updated adapter, the next logical step is to restart the server so the new adapter is loaded. However, the system does not expose a direct restart command via the API; instead, the typical workflow is to “wake up” an agent, which will cause the server to reload its configuration and, if a restart is pending, apply it.

The CEO agent (ID d027bfa7-6d38-412b-94a7-1766519a20da) is the one that was previously blocked on GLI-19. By sending a wakeup request with a source of “on_demand” and a reason indicating we are resuming work on the blocked task, the server will attempt to restart the agent, thereby picking up the newly installed adapter and clearing the timeout issue. The wakeup endpoint returns the full agent object; extracting the `id` field confirms the operation succeeded.

Thus, the appropriate next action is to issue a Bash command that posts to the `/api/agents/<CEO_ID>/wakeup` endpoint with the required JSON payload, captures the response, and prints the agent’s `id`. This will both trigger the restart and give a concise confirmation that the CEO agent is back online.

Proceed with that command.

arguments.command: AID=d027bfa7-6d38-412b-94a7-1766519a20da; R=$(curl -s -m15 -X POST "http://localhost:3100/api/agents/$AID/wakeup" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"source":"on_demand","reason":"Resume work on blocked task GLI-19."}'); echo "$R" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])"
